producer_report.summary:
I added the two defaults `pinned-versions` and `explicit-tool-paths` to defaults.toml and raised the reader budget from 2000 to 2200 tokens. The budgets, policy and pin tests pass. I did not run fmt, clippy or the full `cargo test`.

Each new rule is a single sentence, so the reader sees all of it. The `pinned-versions` line names `claude_version`, `never float`, the `cargo run -p xtask -- repin` command and the refusal. The `explicit-tool-paths` line covers explicit paths, recording which tool ran, and a silent fallback being a defect. Both are marked prose-only. No existing default was touched.

The two new lines take the reader set from 1997 to 2189 estimated tokens, so 2200 is the smallest multiple of 50 that fits. The new figure is in docs/system-facts.md, docs/design/context-engineer.md and run_pin_tests.rs, and CHANGELOG.md has an entry with the old and new budget and the reason.

There are two new tests in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs:
- **New rules:** one asserts that the rendered `defaults().render()` text holds every phrase of both rules.
- **Existing defaults:** one pins all 16 earlier rendered lines verbatim, so any change to them fails.

checks_run.note: 9 passed, including the two new tests, every_role_set_is_within_its_budget and system_facts_budgets_match_computed
64 passed, including the reader headroom run_pin test

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml gains a [[default]] with id "pinned-versions" whose statement is ONE sentence (no '. ' inside) saying config version pins such as claude_version stay exact and never float, are bumped only by `cargo run -p xtask -- repin`, and a refusal from a mismatch names that command, marked prose-only. Check with Grep on defaults.toml.
criteria_check.evidence: Appended entry pinned-versions in defaults.toml. Its statement has no period-space and carries all the halves. The new reader-context test asserts each phrase on the rendered line and passes.

criteria_check.criterion: defaults.toml gains a [[default]] with id "explicit-tool-paths" whose statement is ONE sentence saying a check never relies on inherited environment or ambient tools, the runner passes every tool path explicitly, output records whether the preferred tool or the fallback ran, and a silent fallback is a defect, marked prose-only. Both entries have applies_to and a source citing this request or job 20261027-044511-kktq. Check with Grep on defaults.toml.
criteria_check.evidence: Appended entry explicit-tool-paths, one sentence. Both entries have applies_to [config, build, code] and a source naming job 20261108-142640-egnb and 20261027-044511-kktq. The new test passes.

criteria_check.criterion: git diff shows no change to the statement, applies_to or source of any existing default in defaults.toml: no sentence splitting or shortening of buy-first, tested, public, verified, lazy-requests, root-cause or behavior-evidence. Only two entries are appended.
criteria_check.evidence: defaults.toml edit only appends after the thrash-stop entry; no existing lines touched.

criteria_check.criterion: A new test in crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs builds defaults().render() from the real defaults.toml and asserts it contains both new ids and the key phrases of every half: 'claude_version', 'xtask -- repin', 'never float', 'explicit', 'fallback', 'defect', and the recorded tool used. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` and see it pass.
criteria_check.evidence: the_reader_context_carries_the_whole_version_pin_and_tool_path_rules asserts these on the rendered line, including 'records whether the preferred tool or the fallback ran'. It passed in the budgets run.

criteria_check.criterion: A second new test asserts the rendered line of every pre-existing default equals its pre-change line (listed verbatim in the test), so any change to an existing default's rendered text fails. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli --test budgets` and see it pass.
criteria_check.evidence: existing_defaults_render_exactly_as_before lists all 16 earlier rendered lines and passed.

criteria_check.criterion: The reader budget in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs is raised only by the smallest round amount that fits, and no other budget changes. docs/system-facts.md, docs/design/context-engineer.md and the hard-coded figure in crates/athena-core/src/run_pin_tests.rs match the new figures. Run `cargo test` and see every_role_set_is_within_its_budget, system_facts_budgets_match_computed and the run_pin test pass.
criteria_check.evidence: Reader budget changed from 2000 to 2200; measured size is 2189, and 2150 would not fit. The docs and run_pin_tests.rs now say 2189 of 2200 or 2200. I ran the budgets test file and the athena-core pin tests, both green; I did not run the full cargo test.

criteria_check.criterion: CHANGELOG.md has an entry for the two defaults that states the old and new reader budget and why it was raised. No other files change beyond the listed deliverables.
criteria_check.evidence: Entry added under Unreleased/Added stating 2000 to 2200, the 1997 and 2189 sizes, and why. Only the seven listed files were edited.

criteria_check.criterion: `cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo test` all pass.

open_issues: Neither policy is enforced in the runner; both entries are prose-only, as the request scoped.
learnings: DefaultsModel::render keeps only each statement's first sentence, which ends at the first period followed by a space.
The two new reader lines add 192 estimated tokens, taking the set from 1997 to 2189.
run_pin_tests.rs hard-codes the reader budget as a literal in its expected line.
desires: A way to run cargo without waiting for a free build slot, which blocked several runs.
